Insurance earnings swing with pricing cycles, claims inflation and storm seasons, so I file this under Cyclicals even though my screen tagged it a Stalwart. Reported growth of 17.07% a year is well above the 10-12% I expect from a Stalwart. A P/E of 7.11 is the real warning. For a cyclical, a low P/E on high earnings is what the top of the cycle looks like. On the numbers I have, PEG is 0.42 and PEGY is 0.38, both in my strong-buy zone, and debt-to-equity of 0.22 is comfortable. What could go wrong: earnings are at a cyclical high and a bad catastrophe year or a pricing downturn compresses them, so the low P/E turns out to be a trap. This snapshot does not report insider activity, institutional ownership, margin trend, cash flow trend or years of earnings consistency, so I could not check those. I own the stock, I am up 19.53% since May, and I keep it while I watch for signs of a peak.

memo.two_minute_drill: LEN is Lennar, a homebuilder. It buys land, builds houses and sells them, so its earnings rise and fall with housing demand and interest rates. That makes it a Cyclical, whatever the screen's heuristic label of Stalwart says. A Stalwart compounds steadily at 10-12%, and a homebuilder does not. The growth case is that housing demand returns and the company keeps selling homes at healthy margins. The snapshot shows a 5-year earnings growth rate of 16.2%, but the 3-year rate is -4.6%, so growth has slowed sharply and earnings are going the wrong way recently. At a P/E of 10.4 the PEG is 0.65 and the PEGY is 0.56, which looks cheap. But a low P/E on a cyclical can mean earnings are near a peak rather than a trough, and the snapshot does not tell me where in the cycle we are. Debt-to-equity is 0.27, which is a solid cushion for a downturn. The dividend yield is 2.63%. What could go wrong is that housing demand keeps softening, earnings keep falling and the low P/E turns out to be a trap. I own 4 shares at $87.61 and the stock is at $83.375, down 4.83% after 109 days. The thesis is not broken, but I cannot confirm that it is improving either.
memo.thesis_en: I own this one, and I call it a cyclical, not the stalwart the screen suggests, because homebuilders live and die by the housing cycle.
